f3_program: collection("nigella.sold_houses", "house", "nigella", source("Nigella sells 3 houses"))
observe(at("nigella.sold_houses.count", "one_month"), 3, "count", source("One month, Nigella sells 3 houses"))
collection("nigella.commissions", "commission", "nigella", source("a 2% commission on every house she sells"))
same(at("nigella.commissions.count", "one_month"), at("nigella.sold_houses.count", "one_month"), source("a 2% commission on every house she sells"))
observe(at("nigella.salary.base", "one_month"), 3000, "dollar", source("a base salary of $3,000 a month"))
percent_of(at("nigella.commissions.each.amount", "one_month"), "nigella.sold_houses.each.price", 2, source("a 2% commission on every house she sells"))

sum_relation(at("nigella.earnings.total", "one_month"), at("nigella.salary.base", "one_month"), at("nigella.commissions.total", "one_month"), source("earns a base salary of $3,000 a month plus a 2% commission on every house she sells"))
observe(at("nigella.earnings.total", "one_month"), 8000, "dollar", source("earns $8,000 total"))
multiple("nigella.sold_houses.house_b.price", "nigella.sold_houses.house_a.price", 3, source("House B costs three times as much as House A"))
offset("nigella.sold_houses.house_c.price", scale("nigella.sold_houses.house_a.price", 2), -110000, "dollar", source("House C cost twice as much as House A minus $110,000"))
query("value", "nigella.sold_houses.house_a.price")
assumptions: House A, House B, and House C are the three houses Nigella sold in the stated month.
The House C clause means twice House A's price, followed by subtracting $110,000.

f3_program: collection("john.daily_intake", "intake_component", "john", source("John eats 3 meals a day"))
collection("john.daily_intake.meals", "meal", "john", source("John eats 3 meals a day"))
observe(at("john.daily_intake.meals.count", "day"), 3, "count", source("John eats 3 meals a day"))
member("john.daily_intake", "john.daily_intake.meals", source("John eats 3 meals a day"))
member("john.daily_intake.meals", "john.breakfast", source("Breakfast is 500 calories"))
observe(at("john.breakfast.calories", "day"), 500, "calorie", source("Breakfast is 500 calories"))
member("john.daily_intake.meals", "john.lunch", source("His lunch contains 25% more calories than that"))
percent_more(at("john.lunch.calories", "day"), at("john.breakfast.calories", "day"), 25, source("His lunch contains 25% more calories than that"))
member("john.daily_intake.meals", "john.dinner", source("His dinner is twice as many calories as lunch"))
multiple(at("john.dinner.calories", "day"), at("john.lunch.calories", "day"), 2, source("His dinner is twice as many calories as lunch"))
collection("john.daily_intake.shakes", "shake", "john", source("3 shakes that are each 300 calories"))
observe(at("john.daily_intake.shakes.count", "day"), 3, "count", source("3 shakes that are each 300 calories"))
observe(at("john.daily_intake.shakes.each.calories", "day"), 300, "calorie", source("each 300 calories"))

product_relation(at("john.daily_intake.shakes.calories.total", "day"), at("john.daily_intake.shakes.count", "day"), at("john.daily_intake.shakes.each.calories", "day"), source("3 shakes that are each 300 calories"))
member("john.daily_intake", "john.daily_intake.shakes", source("He also has 3 shakes that are each 300 calories"))
query("sum", "john.daily_intake", "day")
assumptions: Breakfast, lunch, and dinner are the three stated daily meals, and all three shakes are consumed that same day.

f3_program: collection("kylie.class.students", "student", "kylie.class", source("The number of students in Kylie's class is 50"))
observe(at("kylie.class.students.count", "particular_test"), 50, "count", source("The number of students in Kylie's class is 50"))

collection("kylie.class.test.score_groups", "student_group", "kylie.class", source("ten students scored 90 marks, 15 scored ten marks fewer than the first ten students, and the rest scored 60 marks each"))
collection("kylie.class.test.score_groups.first_ten_students", "student", "kylie.class", source("ten students scored 90 marks"))
observe(at("kylie.class.test.score_groups.first_ten_students.count", "particular_test"), 10, "count", source("ten students scored 90 marks"))
observe(at("kylie.class.test.score_groups.first_ten_students.each.test_mark", "particular_test"), 90, "mark", source("ten students scored 90 marks"))
collection("kylie.class.test.score_groups.next_fifteen_students", "student", "kylie.class", source("15 scored ten marks fewer than the first ten students"))
observe(at("kylie.class.test.score_groups.next_fifteen_students.count", "particular_test"), 15, "count", source("15 scored ten marks fewer than the first ten students"))

offset(at("kylie.class.test.score_groups.next_fifteen_students.each.test_mark", "particular_test"), at("kylie.class.test.score_groups.first_ten_students.each.test_mark", "particular_test"), -10, "mark", source("15 scored ten marks fewer than the first ten students"))
collection("kylie.class.test.score_groups.remaining_students", "student", "kylie.class", source("the rest scored 60 marks each"))
observe(at("kylie.class.test.score_groups.remaining_students.each.test_mark", "particular_test"), 60, "mark", source("the rest scored 60 marks each"))
member("kylie.class.test.score_groups", "kylie.class.test.score_groups.first_ten_students", source("ten students scored 90 marks"))
member("kylie.class.test.score_groups", "kylie.class.test.score_groups.next_fifteen_students", source("15 scored ten marks fewer than the first ten students"))
member("kylie.class.test.score_groups", "kylie.class.test.score_groups.remaining_students", source("the rest scored 60 marks each"))
partition("kylie.class.test.score_groups", "kylie.class.students", source("ten students scored 90 marks, 15 scored ten marks fewer than the first ten students, and the rest scored 60 marks each"))
query("mean", at("kylie.class.students.each.test_mark", "particular_test"))
assumptions: The three score groups are disjoint and exhaust the 50 students; “the rest” denotes the complement of the first two groups.

f3_program: collection("sister_party.inflated_balloons", "balloon", "sister_party", source("balloons for her sister’s party"))
observe(at("kris.balloon_inflation.duration", "session"), 30, "minute", source("She has 30 minutes to blow up as many balloons as possible"))
observe(at("kris.balloon_inflation.rate", "session"), 2, "balloon_per_minute", source("Kris can blow up a total of 2 balloon per minute"))
multiple(at("kris.brother.balloon_inflation.rate", "first_15_minutes"), at("kris.balloon_inflation.rate", "session"), 2, source("her brother works twice as fast"))
observe(at("kris.brother.balloon_inflation.duration", "first_15_minutes"), 15, "minute", source("After 15 minutes"))
multiple(at("kris.brother.balloon_inflation.rate", "remaining_15_minutes"), at("kris.brother.balloon_inflation.rate", "first_15_minutes"), 2, source("her brother doubles his speed"))
observe(at("kris.brother.balloon_inflation.duration", "remaining_15_minutes"), 15, "minute", source("the remaining 15 minutes"))

rate_relation(at("kris.balloons.produced.count", "session"), at("kris.balloon_inflation.rate", "session"), at("kris.balloon_inflation.duration", "session"), source("She has 30 minutes to blow up as many balloons as possible and decides to enlist her brother’s help to increase the number of balloons. Kris can blow up a total of 2 balloon per minute"))

rate_relation(at("kris.brother.balloons.produced.count", "first_15_minutes"), at("kris.brother.balloon_inflation.rate", "first_15_minutes"), at("kris.brother.balloon_inflation.duration", "first_15_minutes"), source("her brother works twice as fast. After 15 minutes, her brother doubles his speed"))

rate_relation(at("kris.brother.balloons.produced.count", "remaining_15_minutes"), at("kris.brother.balloon_inflation.rate", "remaining_15_minutes"), at("kris.brother.balloon_inflation.duration", "remaining_15_minutes"), source("her brother doubles his speed and works at this new speed for the remaining 15 minutes"))

produce("kris_balloon_inflation", "kris", at("sister_party.inflated_balloons.count", "current"), at("kris.balloons.produced.count", "session"), source("Kris can blow up a total of 2 balloon per minute"))

produce("brother_first_15_minutes_balloon_inflation", "kris.brother", at("sister_party.inflated_balloons.count", "current"), at("kris.brother.balloons.produced.count", "first_15_minutes"), source("her brother works twice as fast"))

produce("brother_remaining_15_minutes_balloon_inflation", "kris.brother", at("sister_party.inflated_balloons.count", "current"), at("kris.brother.balloons.produced.count", "remaining_15_minutes"), source("her brother doubles his speed and works at this new speed for the remaining 15 minutes"))
query("sum", "sister_party.inflated_balloons", "after_30_minutes")
assumptions: The typo “blowing u balloons” means “blowing up balloons.”
Kris works throughout the 30-minute session, while her brother works at his initial rate for the first 15 minutes and at his doubled rate for the remaining 15 minutes.

f3_program: collection("facebook.productivity_bonus.recipients", "employee", "facebook", source("all its female employees who are mothers"))
collection("facebook.employees", "employee", "facebook", source("Facebook employs 3300 employees"))
observe(at("facebook.employees.count", "current"), 3300, "count", source("Facebook employs 3300 employees"))
collection("facebook.employee_gender_groups", "employee_group", "facebook", source("one-third are men, and of the women"))
collection("facebook.employees.men", "employee", "facebook", source("one-third are men"))
collection("facebook.employees.women", "employee", "facebook", source("of the women, 1200 are not mothers"))
member("facebook.employee_gender_groups", "facebook.employees.men", source("one-third are men"))
member("facebook.employee_gender_groups", "facebook.employees.women", source("of the women"))
partition("facebook.employee_gender_groups", "facebook.employees", source("one-third are men, and of the women"))
fraction_of(at("facebook.employees.men.count", "current"), at("facebook.employees.count", "current"), 1, 3, source("one-third are men"))
collection("facebook.employees.women.motherhood_groups", "employee_group", "facebook", source("of the women, 1200 are not mothers"))
collection("facebook.employees.women.mothers", "employee", "facebook", source("female employees who are mothers"))
collection("facebook.employees.women.non_mothers", "employee", "facebook", source("of the women, 1200 are not mothers"))
member("facebook.employees.women.motherhood_groups", "facebook.employees.women.mothers", source("female employees who are mothers"))
member("facebook.employees.women.motherhood_groups", "facebook.employees.women.non_mothers", source("1200 are not mothers"))
partition("facebook.employees.women.motherhood_groups", "facebook.employees.women", source("of the women, 1200 are not mothers"))
observe(at("facebook.employees.women.non_mothers.count", "current"), 1200, "count", source("1200 are not mothers"))
same("facebook.productivity_bonus.recipients", "facebook.employees.women.mothers", source("all its female employees who are mothers"))
observe(at("facebook.annual_earnings", "2020"), 5000000, "dollar", source("$5,000,000 for the year 2020"))
percent_of(at("facebook.productivity_bonus.total", "2020"), at("facebook.annual_earnings", "2020"), 25, source("This productivity bonus will total 25% of Facebook's annual earnings"))

transfer("facebook_productivity_bonus_award", "facebook", "facebook", "facebook.productivity_bonus.recipients", at("facebook.productivity_bonus.total", "2020"), source("Facebook decided to award a productivity bonus to all its female employees who are mothers"))

quotient_relation(at("facebook.productivity_bonus.per_female_mother", "2020"), at("facebook.productivity_bonus.total", "2020"), at("facebook.employees.women.mothers.count", "current"), source("each female mother employee received, assuming each one received an equal amount"))
query("value", at("facebook.productivity_bonus.per_female_mother", "2020"))
assumptions: The employee categories “men” and “women” are exhaustive for the stated workforce, and the women are partitioned exhaustively into mothers and non-mothers.
The stated employee counts describe the recipient pool for the 2020 bonus.
